requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: The SuperSet matching mechanism IS denoted by the keyword `superset`.
requirements.original: _SuperSet is denoted by the keyword superset.

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: SuperSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains at least all of the elements defined within the SuperSet, and possibly more.
requirements.original: SuperSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values_ contains at least all of the elements defined within the SuperSet, and may contain more.

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: SuperSet SHALL produce a successful match only if there exists a one-to-one mapping from the SuperSet elements to elements of the set of values such that each SuperSet element matches the element it is mapped to.
requirements.original: The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the SuperSet elements to the elements of the set of values where each SuperSet element matches the element of set of values it is mapped to.

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: A SuperSet MAY contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction, and matching mechanisms subject to the restrictions of clause B.1.2.6.
requirements.original: The SuperSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length matching attribute MAY be attached to a SuperSet as a whole.
requirements.original: However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the _SuperSet itself._

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: A set of values matched by a SuperSet contains at least as many elements as the SuperSet (implicit length restriction).
requirements.original: NOTE: The SuperSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values, i.e. the set of values contains at least as many elements as the SuperSet template in order to produce a successful match.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: An `all from` clause MAY be used in a SuperSet to add all elements of a record of or set of template.
requirements.original: Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SuperSets using an all from clause._

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: SuperSet SHALL be used only on values of set of types.
requirements.original: a) SuperSet is an operation for matching that shall be used only on values of set of types.

ambiguity.issue: SuperSet is called an 'operation for matching' although it is a matching mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: Each individual member of a SuperSet's argument SHALL be of the member type of the associated set of type.
requirements.original: b) Individual members of the SuperSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.

ambiguity.issue: 'type replicated by the set of' is used for the member type of the set of type.

improper_terms.used: type replicated by the set of
improper_terms.proper: member type of the set of type

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The member type of the set of type associated with a SuperSet and the member type of the template referenced in an `all from` clause of that SuperSet SHALL be compatible.
requirements.original: c) The member type of the set of associated with the SuperSet template and the member type of the template in the all from clause shall be compatible.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
requirements.original: d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a specific value or combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: An element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute except those prohibited by restriction e) of clause B.1.2.6.
requirements.original: Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SuperSet's argument and an element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet SHALL NOT be `omit`, SuperSet, SubSet, a length restriction or `ifpresent`.
requirements.original: e) The individual members of the SuperSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SuperSet's argument SHALL NOT resolve to AnyValueOrNone.
requirements.original: In addition, the individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SuperSet SHALL NOT resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.original: individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.condition: a length matching attribute is attached to the SuperSet
requirements.canonical: If a length matching attribute is attached to a SuperSet, the minimal length allowed by the length attribute SHALL NOT be less than the number of elements in the SuperSet.
requirements.original: f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SuperSet, the minimal length allowed by the length attribute shall not be less than the number of the elements in the SuperSet.

requirements.subject: ent:superset
requirements.canonical: A template in a SuperSet's argument SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.original: g) Templates in SuperSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: The SubSet matching mechanism IS denoted by the keyword `subset`.
requirements.original: _SubSet is denoted by the keyword subset.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: SubSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains only elements defined within the SubSet, and possibly fewer.
requirements.original: SubSet matches a set of values if, and only if, the set of values contains_ only elements defined within the SubSet, and may contain less.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: SubSet SHALL produce a successful match only if there exists a one-to-one mapping from the elements of the set of values to the SubSet elements such that each element of the set of values is matched by the SubSet element it is mapped to.
requirements.original: The successful match shall be produced only if there exists such a one-to-one mapping from the elements of the set of values to the SubSet elements where each element of the set of values is matched by the SubSet element it is mapped to.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: A SubSet MAY contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction, and matching mechanisms subject to the restrictions of clause B.1.2.7.
requirements.original: The SubSet matching mechanism may contain templates (including template variables) obeying the present template restriction (see clause 15.8) and matching mechanisms with the restrictions given below.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length matching attribute MAY be attached to a SubSet as a whole.
requirements.original: However, the length matching attribute may be attached to the SubSet itself.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: A set of values SHALL contain at most as many elements as the SubSet in order to be matched by the SubSet (implicit length restriction).
requirements.original: The SubSet matching mechanism imposes an implicit length restriction on the matched set of values: the set of values shall contain at most as many elements as the SubSet template in order to produce a successful match.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: An `all from` clause MAY be used in a SubSet to add all elements of a record of or set of template.
requirements.original: Besides specifying individual values, it is possible to add all elements of a record of or set of template into _SubSets using an all from clause._

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: SubSet SHALL be used only on values of set of types.
requirements.original: a) SubSet is an operation for matching that can be used only on values of set of types.

ambiguity.issue: SubSet is called an 'operation for matching' although it is a matching mechanism; 'can be used only' is normalized to SHALL.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: Each individual member of a SubSet's argument SHALL be of the member type of the associated set of type.
requirements.original: b) Individual members of the SubSet's argument shall be of the type replicated by the set of.

ambiguity.issue: 'type replicated by the set of' is used for the member type of the set of type.

improper_terms.used: type replicated by the set of
improper_terms.proper: member type of the set of type

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The member type of the set of type associated with a SubSet and the member type of the template referenced in an `all from` clause of that SubSet SHALL be compatible.
requirements.original: c) The member type of the set of type associated with the SubSet and the member type of the template in the allfrom clause shall be compatible.

requirements.subject: ent:all-from-clause
requirements.canonical: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
requirements.original: d) The template in the all from clause shall resolve either into a matching mechanism or combined template.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'a matching mechanism or combined template', whereas the corresponding restrictions for template list, complement and SuperSet say 'a specific value or combined template', and EXAMPLE 2 of B.1.2.1/B.1.2.2 shows that an all from template resolving into a matching mechanism as a whole is an error. The 'specific value' reading is chosen as the likely intent.
readings: The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a specific value or a combined template.
The template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL resolve either into a matching mechanism or a combined template.

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: An element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet MAY contain any matching mechanism or matching attribute except those prohibited by restriction e) of clause B.1.2.7.
requirements.original: Elements of the combined template may contain any of the matching mechanisms or matching attributes with the exception of those described in the following restriction.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SubSet's argument and an element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL NOT be `omit`, SuperSet, SubSet, a length restriction or `ifpresent`.
requirements.original: e) The individual members of the SubSet's argument and the elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not be the matching mechanisms omit, SuperSet, SubSet and the matching attributes (length restriction and ifpresent).

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: An individual member of a SubSet's argument SHALL NOT resolve to AnyValueOrNone.
requirements.original: In addition, individual members shall not resolve to AnyValueOrNone

requirements.subject: ent:combined-template
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a combined template referenced in an `all from` clause of a SubSet SHALL NOT resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.
requirements.original: individual elements of the combined template in the all from clause shall not resolve to AnyElementsOrNone or permutation.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.condition: a length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet
requirements.canonical: If a length matching attribute is attached to a SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute SHALL NOT exceed the number of elements in the SubSet.
requirements.original: f) If the length matching attribute is attached to the SubSet, the maximum length allowed by the length attribute shall not exceed the number of the elements in the SubSet.

requirements.subject: ent:subset
requirements.canonical: A template in a SubSet's argument SHALL obey the present template restriction.
requirements.original: g) Templates in SubSet's argument shall obey the present template restriction (see clause 15.8).

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: The keyword `omit` IS the notation denoting that an optional field of a record or set, or a specific key within a map, is absent.
requirements.original: The keyword omit denotes that an optional field of a record or set or a specific key within a map shall be absent.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: When used as a matching mechanism, `omit` matches an optional field or a map key if, and only if, the field or key is absent.
requirements.original: If used as a matching mechanism, it matches an optional field or a map key if and only if it is absent.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: `omit` MAY be assigned to a template of any type as a whole, to an optional field of a set or record template, or to a value associated with a key of a map template.
requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: `omit` SHALL NOT be assigned to a mandatory field of a record or set template.
requirements.original: a) It can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of set or record templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: At the time of matching during a receiving operation, `omit` SHALL be applied only to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates.
requirements.original: b) At the time of matching during a receiving operation, it shall be applied to optional fields of record and set templates or to values associated with keys of map templates only.

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether a template that is `omit` as a whole (allowed by restriction a) may be used directly in a receiving operation, and whether a violation is a compile-time or a runtime error. The reading that a top-level `omit` is not allowed in a receiving operation is chosen.
readings: A template that is `omit` as a whole SHALL NOT be used as the top-level template of a receiving operation.
A template that is `omit` as a whole MAY be used in a receiving operation only when referenced from an optional field or map value; otherwise the matching causes a runtime error.
